title: Sanlam Cape Town Marathon — Event Transport Guide (2026)
claims: Free shuttles serve the Expo, start and finish from V&A Waterfront, CTICC, and Civic Centre & Thibault; Sunday start service runs 05:30–06:45 and Sunday return service runs 11:00–17:30.
There is no V&A Waterfront shuttle to the marathon start on Sunday morning.
From Cape Town Station it is a 10-minute walk to Thibault MyCiTi Station, followed by a free shuttle to the stadium; the page links an official PRASA train schedule PDF.
Canal Walk and UCT paid shuttles cost R10 and run on Sunday 24 May only, with first buses at 05:30, last buses at 06:30, and returns from 11:00 to 17:30.
The V&A Waterfront has more than 7,500 open-air and underground parking bays, with shuttle stops at Waterfront, Aquarium, Marina and Silo.
CTICC P1 is accessed from Buitengracht Street, Lower Long Street or FW de Klerk Boulevard; Civic Centre parking is free on Sunday with entrances on Hertzog Boulevard and Civic Avenue.
Green Point P9 is available only on Thursday and Friday, while P12 and P13 are available Thursday to Saturday but not Sunday.
Beach Road and Portswood Road are closed to crossing after 07:30 on Sunday because the wheelchair race starts at 07:50; pedestrian marshals are in place from 05:00.
The free bicycle park is at P4 near the Stadium start.
The MyCiTi Myconnect card costs R40 at kiosks, and road closures affect MyCiTi services on the race weekend.
The transport page includes e-hailing points for the CBD and Green Point and names Uber as an e-hailing service.
